# Observability for AI agents

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric emits metrics, traces, and logs for model calls, tool calls, and policy decisions. The AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecars produce these signals without tracing SDKs in your applications. Measures of business success, such as task completion, also need outcomes that your application supplies.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To set up tracing, refer to [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

Each component reports only what it can observe. For example, the AI Inference Gateway sees model requests and responses, but it cannot tell whether a tool call succeeded or whether the agent finished its task.

The following table lists the signals and where to collect them:

| Signal | Source | Default | Where to collect it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway metrics | AI Inference Gateway | On | Prometheus scrape at `/metrics`, port `9090` by default. Optional export over OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP). |
| Gateway traces | AI Inference Gateway | Off | OTLP export to an OpenTelemetry Collector |
| Tool payload spans | MCP Sidecar | Refer to [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation) | OTLP export to an OpenTelemetry Collector |
| Network spans | Envoy | Off | Consul [distributed tracing](/consul/docs/observe/distributed-tracing) |
| Credential health events | Credential Injection Processor | On | Container logs. Refer to [Verify the configuration](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection/configure#verify-the-configuration). |

Telemetry is best effort. A misconfigured or unreachable telemetry destination degrades that signal but does not change the request outcome.

## Metrics and traces

Metrics and traces answer different questions:

| Signal | Use it for | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metrics | Traffic, latency, errors, token usage, and policy outcomes in aggregate | Aggregation and delivery loss make metrics unsuitable as a billing ledger. |
| Traces | Following one request or workflow across agents, gateways, and tools | Sampling and incomplete instrumentation limit what a trace shows. |

Gateway metrics cover request outcomes, stage duration, token usage, streaming, identity resolution, and PII processing. PII metrics record the detector type and action, never the detected value.

<!-- TODO: List the gateway metric names. The processor in the csl-inf-rt codebase defines them. -->

Traces cover the gateway and tool-call paths. Applications forward trace context so that proxy spans join one workflow trace. They do not emit spans themselves. Traces do not show an agent's internal reasoning, the business logic inside a tool, or whether a task succeeded. To learn how spans are produced, refer to [Auto-instrumentation for AI agents](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation).

[Cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) uses these traces to find agents that repeat the same tool call with the same arguments. Collecting traces does not turn on enforcement. Cycle detection also needs Agentic Analytics.

## Correlation and model attribution

Request IDs and trace IDs connect observations across processing stages, including the gateway's processing before and after routing. A request ID is a join key. It is not a workload identity or a credential.

The requested model and the model that served the request can differ, for example after failover. Keep both where available, and tie retry and fallback evidence to the attempt it belongs to.

## Audit trail

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric does not include a compliance audit trail. Metrics and traces are operational evidence, not a durable or tamper-evident record. Audit retention, access control, integrity, and delivery remain your responsibility.

## Calculate metrics and KPIs

Auto-instrumentation supplies observations, not finished metrics or key performance indicators (KPIs). The following tables are guidance for your metrics or analytics backend. They are not built-in metric names.

### Operational metrics

| Measure | Inputs | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request rate | Logical model requests or tool calls over a time window | Count each exchange once, not each network, payload, and processor span. |
| Protocol error rate | Failed exchanges divided by all exchanges in the same population and window | Include tool and JSON-RPC errors. HTTP success alone does not show tool success. |
| Request latency | Request durations as distributions or percentiles for one observation point | Do not mix Envoy timing with processor timing, or add sibling spans as sequential work. |
| Token usage | Usage reported in model responses, by model and request | Treat missing usage as unknown, not zero. Count a response observed on both sides of a gateway once. |

Before you compare results, define the observation point, denominator, time window, and how you treat retries. Sampled traces describe only the sampled traffic, so use request counters for totals.

### Higher-order KPIs

These KPIs combine proxy observations with outcomes that your application defines.

| KPI | Inputs | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task completion rate | Application-defined task starts, outcomes, and correlation across calls | Successful requests or model responses do not prove task completion. |
| Tool success rate | Tool protocol outcomes and application-defined business results | A protocol success can still be a failed business operation. |
| Cost per successful task | Attributed usage, current provider pricing, and confirmed task outcomes | Missing usage, retries, pricing changes, and incomplete tasks skew the result. |
| Autonomous versus escalated outcomes | Application approval events and final task outcomes | An approval request or timeout is not a completed task. |
| Model quality or routing effectiveness | Application evaluations and the model that served each request | Latency, token counts, and availability do not measure quality. |

Keep cost estimates separate from your provider's invoice.

## Best practices

- Keep metric labels bounded. Never use request IDs, trace IDs, user IDs, full workload identities, arbitrary paths, or request content as labels. Unbounded labels raise memory use and can expose sensitive data.
- Keep prompts, responses, tool arguments, and tool results out of metrics and logs. Payload traces that carry content need approval and redaction. Refer to [Payload span sensitive data security](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation#payload-span-sensitive-data-security).
- Record bounded error categories instead of raw provider error messages, which can contain request data.
- Restrict access to and retention of telemetry metadata, such as identities, model usage, and policy decisions, even when content capture is off.
